relations.note: Agricola calls Rauni “Ukko’s woman”; her action precedes Ukko’s powerful thundering.
Later pantheon-builders made Akka Ukko’s wife from paired common nouns and Sámi comparisons.
Väinämöinen invokes Ukko for rain, healing, protection, weather, and help completing tasks.
Ilmarinen invokes Ukko to provide snow and cool destructive fire.

relations.myth: Origins of iron and celestial fire
relations.note: Regional variants redistribute atmospheric, smithing, iron, and fire-making functions between Ukko and Ilmarinen.
Ukko answers Lemminkäinen by opening heaven and sending iron hail against the fiery horse.
Ukko sends iron hail against Hiisi’s fiery horse and opposes harmful beings with celestial weapons.
After Louhi conceals the luminaries, Ukko’s celestial fire aids attempts to restore light.

relations.myth: Lost celestial fire and darkened sun
relations.note: Ukko participates in varying narratives about celestial fire and restoration of the darkened sun.
Ukko is indirectly connected with restoring the moon after Louhi conceals the luminaries.
Ilmatar appeals to Ukko for release from pregnancy, but he does not answer directly.
Ukko produces three maidens from his hands and knee; their milk becomes forms of iron.
Writers equated their analogous thunder functions, although no native narrative meeting is recorded.
Comparative scholarship links Ukko with Baltic thunder gods through shared structures and Perkele’s etymology.
Ukko’s titles and Jumala formulas overlap under Christian influence, sometimes approaching monotheistic language.
